summary: The 900 s run matches the required sequence and all listed checks pass on the reported results. Tank 1 filled from 0.05 m to 0.80 m, transfer began only after that high level and the 10 s wait, STOP at 220 s closed all valves and START at 280 s resumed transfer rather than restarting fill, Tank 2 drained to low and the controller restarted filling after the 8 s inter-cycle wait, the second STOP kept all valves closed until SHUT at 700 s, shutdown opened V2 and V3 together with V1 closed, and shutdown completed at 713.33 s with both tanks low before the controller returned to IDLE and stayed there through 900 s.
assumptions: Numeric state reporting code assumption retained: IDLE=0, FILL_T1=1, WAIT_AFTER_FILL=2, TRANSFER_T1_T2=3, WAIT_AFTER_TRANSFER=4, DRAIN_T2=5, WAIT_AFTER_DRAIN=6, PAUSED=7, SHUTDOWN=8.
Simulation horizon/output-grid assumption retained: 900 s horizon with 9000 output intervals to represent 0.1 s scan/update behavior on the result grid.
Exact-time evaluation assumption retained: checks at scheduled times are evaluated at the stated schedule instants directly, without adding an extra machine-evaluable +/-2 s slack window.
Plant-physics assumption retained: the model uses the explicit constant-cross-section level-balance equations from the legacy note rather than a head-dependent hydraulic network.
Valve-stroking assumption retained: 0.8 s open and 0.6 s close stroke times are not converted into partial-opening flow dynamics; valve commands act as binary flow enable signals.
Command-pulse assumption retained: momentary command pulse width is 0.2 s so the 0.1 s PLC scan can observe each scheduled command.
Drain-floor assumption retained: a 1e-6 m physical floor is used only in the T2 drain cutoff condition to avoid negative level.
Non-negative inventory assumption retained: transfer outflow from TK-101 is cut off when tank1_level_m <= 0.

Further inferred from parameter values: the simulated process uses fixed nominal flows qFill=0.0060 m^3/s, qTransfer=0.0045 m^3/s, qDrain=0.0050 m^3/s independent of liquid head, because the observed level slopes remain piecewise constant at 0.005, -0.00375, 0.003214, -0.003571, and -0.000357 m/s according to which valve commands are active.
